steps.content: [Is the Speaker of the City Council Driving DisCity's Future Off a Cliff?]

steps.speaker: Anchor A
steps.content: Speaker Max King was spotted vacationing at a seaside resort with a mysterious Outlander woman. Analysts say the trip could signal a growing alignment with Fraser. Professor, what's your take?

steps.speaker: Professor B
steps.content: It's a rather unusual move. Our analysis suggests that he's sending a clear message with the public display: Pledge your allegiance, and even someone from Fraser can earn a place among DisCity's elite. We've seen this playbook before in his grandfather's era.

steps.speaker: Anchor A
steps.content: You mean Ronald King and the former Commander? Ms. Maris's alliance would decide which side gained the satellite town's support. Rumor has it those two old friends on the establishment side spent their lives competing, yet neither ever won. Ms. Maris never took a side.

steps.speaker: Professor B
steps.content: My deepest respects to Ms. Maris. She never let political winds sway her convictions, dedicating her entire life to the fight against Mania. It is high time DisCity's politicians study the examples set by their predecessors. After all, only by learning from history can we build a better future!

steps.speaker: Anchor A
steps.content: For more on Ms. Maris, stay tuned for our special feature, The Life of Maris Andre. We'll be right back after the break...

steps.speaker: Anchor C
steps.content: This tip comes from an arms-dealing family descendant, and the truth may come as a shock to some of you: In the age of Mania weapons, the Andohar family is nearing bankruptcy. General Augustus’s lavish lifestyle, military expenses, and image maintenance have finally caught up with her.

steps.speaker: Anchor C
steps.content: Because of this, she is reportedly exploring new revenue streams. According to an insider tip, Shattered Blade commemorative coins and autographs of the General herself are already in production... with the first limited release consisting of 40,000 sets!

steps.speaker: Anchor D
steps.content: This is not an easy thing to admit, but yes, my friends, Marshal Dravyn was my biological grandfather. You only need to look at my gray eyes and hair to see the connection. My grandmother often told me stories of the time he spent at her estate during ceasefires many years ago.

steps.speaker: Anchor D
steps.content: The attic was prepared specifically for the Marshal. My grandmother was the daughter of a manor owner, a true country girl at heart. She loved climbing trees and scaling walls. That's why there's a little balcony up there. That's where they would always meet in the moonlight...

steps.speaker: Anchor E
steps.content: Don't miss today's juicy scoop! Why has the West District remained out of reach for so long? And which Paradeisos factions are so formidable that even the Cavendish family has to tread carefully around them? Drop me a couple of coins and I'll break it all down for you...
You turn off the screen displaying a diagram illustrating the Kervoz family's romantic histories, rubbing your aching eyes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...What was I watching?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Since the return of the DisCorps, the public's interest in conspiracy theories has been on the rise, fueling the popularity of this kind of "debunking" content. People no longer place their trust in textbooks or official records. Instead, they seek to challenge established narratives, expose the corruption of the ruling elite, and uncover the true history of this era.

options: This is what they call history?
This is what they call the truth?

choices.text: This is what they call history?
This is what they call the truth?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Many believe so. Judging from the current situation, the movement has clearly spiraled out of control. Sensationalized, fabricated stories are flooding even mainstream channels, and the misinformation they spread is seeping into every sector.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The MBCC received a request for assistance claiming that Mania influence was behind this phenomenon, but our investigation has found no such connection so far. It may simply be an excuse to borrow the bureau's manpower due to their own staffing shortages...

You silently scan the report in your hands. It involves a wide range of parties. Besides the Public Security Bureau, municipal departments, and the military, even a few voices from Paradeisos have called for this matter to be addressed...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Not a bad reason to get involved, actually.
You think it over, then turn off the screen in front of you, standing up.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm heading to EDGE.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...That's the current situation. Regarding this request for assistance, the MBCC's own archives contain limited documents, and this case clearly entails cross-referencing a large amount of DisCity's historical records.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We're all aware of how much of a hassle data access requests can be. Given the scale of this investigation, broader access clearance would help ensure a smoother process.
Schorl takes in your request, the light beams across its surface flickering.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: The scope of information you're interested in spans quite a range of categories, Chief, and the access permissions involved are... let's call it a labyrinth. My current module set isn't really built to navigate that gracefully. Fortunately, there's a dedicated institution designed to field requests like yours.
Just as you mentally prepare to have your request brushed off once again, Schorl's response takes an unexpected turn.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: EDGE has granted you a special information security clearance, so you'll now have high-level access to the <color=#fb9259>DisCity Central Library</color>. Beyond borrowing books or films you might enjoy, you'll be able to pull extensive backups of EDGE data.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: You'll also find exceptional professionals there who can provide the help you need. I'm confident they'll earn your trust.
You receive an incomplete dossier on your personal device.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Celine Fabius is a scholar of considerable renown in academic circles. She also serves, by EDGE's commission, as our city-state's specially appointed <color=#fb9259>chronicler</color>, in charge of collecting, recording, enriching, and preserving our history from every conceivable angle.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Her family holds deep roots in Paradeisos, which has left her with no shortage of connections. Yet despite her abundant resources, she maintains the integrity and restraint expected of a chronicler and witness. Quite admirable, if you ask me.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: The professor's grasp of DisCity's history—as well as the social, economic, and political currents beneath it—runs deep. Her standing is unimpeachable. I do hope she'll provide the assistance you require.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This dossier lists her as a Sinner from Paradeisos, but why is almost every field left blank here?

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Her ability is non-combat in nature, so she poses virtually no threat. She is effectively no different from an ordinary person, which is why registration was never required. Perhaps you could use this opportunity to establish contact with her.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Non-combat ability? What exactly does it do?

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Apparently, she has an <color=#fb9259>excellent memory</color>.

A few days pass. Just as online armchair historians drop their latest bombshell—that Speaker Max King is actually Speaker Stewart's secret illegitimate brother—you receive a notification that the historian is already waiting in the MBCC interrogation room.

With a cascade of jet-black hair and ice-blue eyes, the scholar before you sits with a calm gaze and composed demeanor. Her hands rest lightly on a blank notebook in her lap, as though she were here for a book club meeting rather than an interrogation.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Nice to meet you, Ms. Celine. Thank you for accepting our invitation. Allow me to introduce myself: I am ${PlayerName}, Chief of the Minos Bureau. I apologize for receiving you here, but please understand this is not a formal interrogation. It'll be just a routine interview followed by a simple registration.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Afterward, we will move to a proper conference room to discuss the fabricated historical accounts that have been circulating online.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Please, don't trouble yourself. This room is fine. Seeking historical truth and correcting the record are simply part of my work. I'll do everything I can to assist with your investigation. My apologies for the delayed registration. I've been tied up with my work at the library.
She offers a polite bow, her smile gentle and humble.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Shall we begin, then?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: According to our records, you're a member of Paradeisos's renowned Fabius family and have served as Head Librarian of the Central Library for the past decade, overseeing DisCity's official historical records. Is that correct?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I see you've done your homework thoroughly. Yes, as the library's historian, my work primarily involves gathering historical materials, overseeing the library's day-to-day operations, and compiling and cataloguing records into the central system.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Over these past ten years, we have compiled a comprehensive history of DisCity, tracing events from Nightfall to the present day. The latest volume will be published shortly. If you happen to be a history buff too, Chief, I do hope you'll pick up a copy.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: And if buying books isn't quite your thing, you're always welcome to register for a library card. A small deposit is all it takes, and you'll have access to a full century of DisCity's history.
Though she sounds perfectly sincere, the DisCity history sitting on the public shelves is not what you are after. As for the data you actually need, you're not certain she can provide it.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Is that how the library keeps its lights on?
You really live up to your reputation as a celebrated scholar.

choices.text: Is that how the library keeps its lights on?
You really live up to your reputation as a celebrated scholar.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Hehe, running a library is unimaginably costly, while the budget Paradeisos provides isn't always enough to cover all the costs. Most of the time, we simply have to come up with ways to pay the bills on our own.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Can't you apply for more funding?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: That would require convincing people that the library's efforts in preserving history and educating the public are more urgent than the industrial crisis, Mania research, or even the Outland War.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Or that it matters more than the birthday dinner party some official's mistress is throwing.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: ...You've got a nice sense of humor, Chief.
Her eyes crinkle as a warm smile spreads across her face.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I'm grateful that you share that view. But it's all right. We've long since made our peace with it.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: This profession existed long before Nightfall. A historian's job is to faithfully document every historical event, to devote oneself to recovering scattered records. And yet, more often than not, we are only allowed to write what pleases those in power, or worse, compelled to fabricate false evidence.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: People need these record keepers to preserve their history, yet they also fear the power of their pens. Poverty, persecution, and even exile are common occupational hazards. Survival becomes especially difficult during times of transition. In fact, the pre-Nightfall records we possess today were once fragments passed down through this river of blood, preserved in the same arduous manner.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Nightfall changed the world beyond recognition, yet our duties of investigation, documentation, compilation, and research remain unchanged. Instead of the tyrants of the past, Mania is now our greatest adversary. As for poverty, oppression, solitude, and temptation, they are obstacles that have never vanished, and never will.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Even so, many of my colleagues gave everything they had, risking their lives to preserve the precious few records that survived, gathering them through whatever channels they could find so that others might one day read them.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: And so, securing funding through various means, keeping the library running, and honoring the sacrifices of those who came before, that is the call of duty the library and I must answer in this age.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Academics are deemed "useless" by many. What a shame. If only these history books were worth as much as Hypercubes...
You shake your head at her words.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're being way too humble. What you do is remarkable.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: During several major incidents in the past, the historical materials provided by the library played a crucial role.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Records about the DisCorps, the metropoles, and even the origins of the West District and Nirvana... Without the help of you and your colleagues, we never could have resolved some of those issues so quickly.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That said, most of this information is locked away in the archives, and ordinary people can never access it. That seems somewhat at odds with what the library stands for.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: My, that's quite a pointed question, Chief.
Not seeming offended by your remark, she simply smiles and explains.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: History is an immensely complex subject. Verified facts, disputed interpretations, and even embellished conjectures are often intertwined. Releasing them all without distinction could easily lead to misuse and misinterpretation, ultimately pushing the public further away from the truth.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: There's an old saying in our field: "Let history be the judge." Many perspectives must stand the test of time before they can truly become part of history. That is why I do not insist that everything be immediately made available to the public. While I wish to reveal the true and accurate account of history, I also feel a responsibility to safeguard against its more chaotic aspects.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But that also leaves the public in the dark, vulnerable to all kinds of misinformation. Which is exactly the problem we're facing right now.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: ...Sigh.
She lets out a slightly theatrical sigh.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I've been keeping a close eye on this situation as well. It's disheartening to see some of my colleagues get caught up in it. The pressures and temptations of this era can change people, and even historians are not immune to such influences.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Are you suggesting a certain expert might be pulling the strings behind all this?
She blinks.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I'm not sure what sort of expert might be behind this, but it would certainly take a great deal of calculation to construct arguments that appear so sound and credible, and that have spread so rapidly and so widely. Isn't that why you came to the library, Chief? Because you had the same thought?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: To be frank, I've been racking my brain over this myself... As a historian, the spread of such fabricated records both irritates and saddens me. However, the library is already understaffed, and we simply don't have the resources to conduct an investigation of our own.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Therefore, I'm very glad to hear the MBCC is willing to take this on.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: There are plenty of young, intellectual minds in the Bureau, after all. I'd hate to see them led astray by this kind of misinformation.
As you speak, you put an investigation report on the desk.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We sifted through a massive amount of data and identified several videos that stood out as particularly suspicious. They cover a wide range of topics, but a number of them feature historians affiliated with the library.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Our conversation has told me everything I need to know about where you stand. You carry yourself with the dignity and integrity of a respectable historian. And I believe you're just as determined as we are to find whoever is behind this.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Hehe... Then I'll gladly accept your trust, Chief.
She nods with a smile, her gaze skimming over those videos before settling on a particular name.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Chief, have you heard of the name Maris Andre?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That woman who will soon be posthumously awarded the DisCity Leader Medal for her efforts against Mania? Of course I've heard of her.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A civilian hero who aided in the Battle of Glory of the Rust, helped establish multiple anti-Mania facilities, and even contributed to the development of Mania detection technology during the MBCC's early days. There's even a biography of her in the Bureau's library. I have no idea how long it's been sitting there.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: But regretfully, <color=#fb9259>Maris Andre never actually existed.</color>

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Of course, this has nothing to do with Mania. Someone has simply wielded their academic influence and fabricated her existence.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Records about her follow a single linear timeline. They are thorough, but not flawless. Nearly every milestone in her life traces back to pre-existing Mania-related events. Her birthplace, related artifacts, portraits, and even her biography only appeared in the public eye after those key events had been established.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: How can you be so certain? Couldn't these so-called flaws be a result of incomplete historical records?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Because... N.F. 103 was a remarkable year. It was the year when the Eclipse Operation failed, the BR-003 crisis erupted, and a humble historian awakened her special power. Yet in this historian's mind, no one by that name ever returned from the Rust since.
Your breath catches.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Oh... Did I surprise you? You invited me here because you had questions about our history, didn't you? And I'm only answering them honestly.
She smiles softly, lowering her gaze. Something in the air has shifted.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: My approach differs slightly from that of other historians. What others record with pen and paper, I can remember after a single glance. And that includes not only the documents indexed in the Grand Library's system, but also the highly classified files that never see the light of day.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Your question about access to the Grand Library's archives was rather tactful, but I could sense the frustration you experienced from these restrictions.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: There's no need to worry. I understand, truly. You seek access to more historical data, and I wish to correct the flood of false information spreading through society. That gives us common ground for a meaningful partnership.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What exactly do you mean by partnership? Are you saying you can help me get higher clearance?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I'm afraid not. If Paradeisos hasn't granted you that clearance, it isn't my place to overstep. After all, I'm just a humble civil servant.
She effortlessly shifts the responsibility back onto EDGE, resting her chin in her hand, a mysterious smile playing at her lips.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: But I can certainly put in an application on your behalf, along with a letter of recommendation. That may help things move along a little more smoothly.
Your heartbeat quickens.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: All I ask in return is that you help me bring Maris Andre's puppet master to justice. A fair trade, wouldn't you say?
She extends a gentle invitation, waiting patiently for your answer.
She already knows it'll be positive.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sure, but there's one thing I don't quite follow. If this has nothing to do with Mania, why come to the MBCC?
At that, she gives you a knowing wink.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: For one thing, you've piqued my curiosity, Chief... I'm about to begin compiling a historical record of the West District, and I was hoping to arrange an in-depth interview with you.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: And for another, I imagine the Bureau is considerably better staffed and funded for this sort of thing than the library.
So that's what it all comes down to, huh...
